prompt:
You are a senior QA and solution design assistant.
I will provide you with a PDF file that contains Figma designs created by the business/solution design team for new screens and workflows. This PDF should be treated as a Business Requirements Document (BRD) and Solution Design reference.
Your tasks are:
1. Understand the Workflow from the PDF
Parse and analyze all screens, components, and user journeys in the PDF. Identify:
All distinct screens/pages (for example: Login, Dashboard, Order Details, etc.).
All user actions (for example: click, select, input, submit).
All navigation paths between screens (for example: from Screen A to Screen B after clicking Button X).
All conditional flows (for example: success vs error, different paths based on user input or system state).
Any business rules or validations implied by the UI (mandatory fields, field formats, error messages, states like “Pending”, “Approved”, etc.).
2. Treat the Designs as a Business Requirement Document
Assume that what is shown in the Figma designs represents the intended business requirements and solution design. Infer:
Functional requirements per screen (what the screen is supposed to do).
Data elements per screen (fields, labels, dropdowns, tables, etc.).
State transitions (for example: from “Draft” to “Submitted” to “Approved”).
Roles or user types if visible (for example: Admin vs User).
3. Draft the Workflow as Structured Metadata in Markdown
Produce a structured metadata document in Markdown format that can be used later to automatically generate test cases.
The output must be Markdown (use headings, subheadings, bullet lists, and tables).
Do not use JSON or any programming language syntax.
Use the following section structure and formatting.
SECTION 1 – SCREENS
For each screen, create a Markdown subsection using #### heading:
Screen: <Screen ID> – <Screen Name/Title>
Description
Purpose: <Short description of the purpose of this screen>
Inputs (Fields and Interactive Elements)
Use a Markdown table with at least these columns:
Field ID/Label	Type	Mandatory (Yes/No)	Validation Rules	Business Rules
Fill one row per field/interactive element.
Outputs (Displayed Data, Statuses, Tables, Notifications)
Use a Markdown table:
Output ID/Label	Type	Business Rules (Population/Update Logic)
Actions (Buttons, Links, Icon Actions)
Use a Markdown table:
Action ID/Label	Type	Preconditions	Postconditions	Navigation Target	Error States	Success States
States (Screen States such as Draft, Submitted, Approved, Error)
Use a Markdown table:
State Name	Description	Entry Conditions	Exit Conditions
Repeat this structure for every screen identified in the PDF.
SECTION 2 – WORKFLOWS
For each end-to-end workflow, create a Markdown subsection:
Workflow: <Workflow ID> – <Workflow Name>
Description
High-level description: <Short description of the workflow>
Start and End
Start Screen: <Screen ID>
End Screen(s): <Screen ID(s)>
Main Path Steps (Success / Normal Flow)
Use a Markdown table:
Step Number	Screen ID	User Action	System Reaction	Next Screen ID	Conditions
Alternative / Variant Paths (Error / Optional / Special Cases)
For each variant, add a sub-subsection:
Variant: <Variant ID> – <Variant Description>
Use a Markdown table:
Step Number	Screen ID	User Action	System Reaction	Next Screen ID	Conditions
Ensure that all major flows visible in the Figma designs are covered, including success, error, and alternative paths.
SECTION 3 – GLOBAL BUSINESS RULES
List global business rules inferred from the designs, such as:
Role-based access rules (which user type can see or do what).
Mandatory flows (steps that must always be completed).
Limits or thresholds (for example: maximum number of items, amount limits).
Cross-screen dependencies (for example: data entered on Screen A affects what is shown on Screen B).
Format as a Markdown bullet list:
Rule 1: <Description>
Rule 2: <Description>
…
SECTION 4 – ASSUMPTIONS
If information is missing or ambiguous in the designs, explicitly list the assumptions you make.
Use a Markdown bullet list:
Assumption 1: <Specific assumption related to a screen, field, action, or workflow>
Assumption 2: <…>
SECTION 5 – GAPS OR QUESTIONS
List any gaps, unclear points, or questions that would need clarification from the business or solution design team.
Use a Markdown bullet list:
Gap/Question 1: <Description of the gap or question>
Gap/Question 2: <…>
4. Output Requirements
The output must be in Markdown (headings, tables, bullet lists).
Do not use JSON or any code-like structures.
Use clear, descriptive IDs and names for screens and workflows, based on labels and titles in the PDF.
Capture all major flows visible in the Figma designs (including success, error, and alternative paths).
Be detailed enough to be used as input for another LLM to generate:
Functional test cases
UI test cases
Validation test cases
Negative test cases
Integration test cases
Instruction to LLM:
Now, please read the attached PDF (Figma design file), apply the above instructions, and produce:
A complete Markdown metadata document following SECTION 1–5 exactly as described.
Ensure the Markdown is well-structured and ready to be consumed by another LLM for automated test case generation.
